articleTitle: A Ku-Band Low-Noise Amplifier in 40-nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper proposes a Ku-band CMOS low-noise amplifier (LNA). It is designed in one-stage cascode topology. The inductive degeneration is used for input as well as noise matching. Fabricated in a 40 nm CMOS technology, it achieves a measured noise figure (NF) of 2.5 dB from 10 to 14 GHz. A measured peak gain of 11 dB is also realized at 11.7 GHz. It consumes 10 mW dc power under 1-V supply and occupies only 0.162 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: A Reconfigurable CNN Accelerator using Tile-by-Tile Computing and Dynamic Adaptive Data Truncation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper proposed a Reconfigurable Neural Accelerator (RNA) for multiple CNNs acceleration. A novel tile-by-tile computing (TTC) model is designed for RNA to fully reuse data between convolutional layers and significantly decrease data transmission, which can substantially reduce memory bandwidth requirement and improve throughput. Besides, an on-line dynamic adaptive data truncation (DADT) mechanism is designed to activate the intermediate result data generated by multiplier, which can compensate accuracy loss from fixed-point operation in RNA. The RNA architecture was implemented on Xilinx XC7VX485 FPGA and working at 200 MHz. Testing results show that the performance of running LeNet, AlexNet and VGG are 400 GOPS, 498 GOPS and 528 GOPS, respectively. The average energy efficiency of RNA is 71.7 GOPS/W at 6.63 W power consumption.

articleTitle: A Low-Cost and High-Throughput Virtual-Channel Router with Arbitration Optimization
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Network-on-chip (NoC) has emerged as an on-chip interconnect technology that overcomes the constraints of traditional bus-based system. Virtual-channel router with transmission priority plays an important role especially in many-core chip multiprocessors (CMP) executing different applications. In this paper, we propose two arbitration optimization methods based on virtual-channel router, consisting of scoring crossbar arbitration and arbitration interception. The design has been implemented on the Xilinx ZCU102 FPGA board, and the results show that our work outperforms the traditional virtual-channel router in the NoC while reducing logic resource by approximately 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> and achieving 2x better performance.

articleTitle: A Small-Signal Model Extraction and Optimization Method for AlGaN/GaN HEMT Up to 110 GHz
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: this paper proposed a small-signal compact model for AlGaN/GaN HEMT up to 110 GHz. In this equivalent circuit the manifold parts of gate and drain are considered to improve the model accuracy at mm-wave frequency. As some extrinsic parameters can't be extracted directly from measurement data in this equivalent circuit, some empirical equations are shown here to generate the initial values. After that an optimization method is used here to decrease the errors between simulation and measurement, the optimization procedure are also shown here. The intrinsic parameters are optimized with the same method. Finally the 0.1 μmAlGaN/GaN HEMT transistors with the gate-width 4x30 μm and 4x50 μm are used to verify the model. Compared with results of other papers, the model errors show in this paper are quite small.

articleTitle: Airport Runway FOD Detection System Based on 77GHz Millimeter Wave Radar Sensor
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Foreign object debris (FOD), like stones and metal fasteners in the airport runway may damage aircraft. Many companies have developed relevant detection systems. However weak radar-cross section (RCS) static and dynamic targets detection is still a problem. This paper proposes time accumulation method to remove background clutter and adaptively detect weak RCS targets using two-dimensional rectangular window function. Then we propose a space-time joint estimation algorithm by introducing subarray delays to achieve high precision and high accuracy target speed and angle.

articleTitle: Integration of mm-wave Antennas on Fan-Out Wafer Level Packaging (FOWLP) for Automotive Radar Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: The integration of mm-wave antennas on fan-out wafer level packaging (FOWLP) for automotive radar applications is presented in this paper. The size of the package is 12 x 15 x 0.45 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The package includes seven antenna arrays realized with three redistribution layers (RDL). Three patch antenna arrays are used as transmitting antennas and four patch antenna arrays are used as receiving antennas. The simulation results show that the proposed antenna achieves a 10-dB input impedance bandwidth of 5.5 GHz and a maximal peak realized gain of 9.9 dBi at 77.6 GHz. The angle resolution of the MIMO radar can be improved to 9.6°.

articleTitle: Developing of Wafer Level Fan-Out Packaging Technology for Millimeter-Wave Chip Using Different Carriers
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: With the fast development of 5G, millimeter wave (mm-Wave) chip packaging technology has broad application in automotive radar, IoT (Internet of Things) and 5G communication. Although quad flat no-lead (QFN) package is widely deployed in radio frequency (RF) and highspeed digital systems, it cannot meet the requirements of electrical performance when the frequency is up to 45 GHz. The demand for mm-Wave chip packaging with high performance, high integration density and low manufacturing cost is increasing rapidly. A number of advanced packaging technologies with fan-out structure emerged over the past years. Recently, the development of fan-out wafer level packaging (FOWLP) has been paid more attention. This paper presents a brief review of the mm-Wave chip packaging solutions which are based on wafer level fan-out packaging technologies including embedded wafer level grid ball array (eWLB), embedded silicon fan out (eSiFO), glass panel embedding (GPE) and embedded glass fan out (eGFO). Besides, the electrical performance of these packages is presented by simulation.

Author Keywords: embedded wafer level ball grid array

articleTitle: The Optimization of Localization and Navigation for Vision-based Robot
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper studies the localization and navigation of vision-based robots. In the first step, obtaining the video stream by the monocular camera to get high-quality image information. Then we do a series of preprocessing, such as noise reduction, space conversion, contour extraction, to extract color and shape information. In the second step, getting edge information using a corner detection algorithm combined with weight assignment and constraint, acquiring the current position using the multi-region multi-threshold edge localization algorithm. In particular, for the multi-object locate problem caused by the change of the robot viewing angle, using multi-image stitching matching algorithm to locate, which based on the spatial intermediate point. The third step, we design a number of basic action groups, robot will select the appropriate action group according to the current position and obstacle information, so the robot can pass quickly by bypassing, rolling or crossing over.

articleTitle: Shielding Effectiveness Measurement of SiP Based on Near-Field Scanning
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper introduces the electromagnetic shielding effectiveness (SE) measurement of the system-in-package (SiP) based on near-field scanning. This method is more flexible compared to the conventional methods. Several key components of this method are introduced, such as near-field scanning platform and the magnetic probe. Measurement of commercial SiPs is performed to show the accuracy of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A 56-Gb/s PAM4 Continuous-Time Linear Equalizer with Fixed Peaking Frequency in 40-nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This design presents a 56-Gb/s PAM4 CTLE in 40-nm CMOS. By adopting capacitive degeneration, inductive peaking, and inverter-based TIA, the two-stage CTLE generates a high-frequency peak which can compensate the gain attenuation due to channel loss at required Nyquist frequency. Through tuning the source degenerated capacitor of the first-stage gm-cell and the feedback inductor of the second-stage inverter-based TIA, the designed CTLE can achieve an 8.6-dB tuning range at the fixed peaking frequency of 22 GHz. The proposed structure reaches a DC-gain at — 0.6 dB from a 1-V voltage supply, which can recover the eye diagram of the 56-Gb/s PAM4 signal from distortion due to the 8.6-dB channel loss at Nyquist frequency.

articleTitle: Analytical Thermal Model for Self-Heating Effects in Advanced FinFET Devices
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: An analytical thermal model for self-heating effects in advanced FinFET devices is proposed in this paper. The heat generation profiles of FinFET under different source/drain doping concentrations and bias voltages are investigated. Based on the curve fitting of heat source distribution of device and the extraction of equivalent lumped thermal resistances, a one-dimensional (1-D) analytical thermal model is developed for efficient simulation of self-heating effects in FinFETs. The accuracy of the proposed model are verified by the commercial solver COMSOL.

articleTitle: Cellular Point-taking Method Applied to Load-Pull
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Aiming at the selection of reflection coefficient points in load-pull, this paper proposes a cellular point-taking method. Compared with conventional sector point-taking method, this new method can cover Smith chart more evenly with same sample points. Load-dependent X-parameter is extracted using both methods, and it shows that the proposed method can improve the model accuracy without increasing the size of the model.

articleTitle: Low Power Clock Tree Optimization by Clock Buffer/Inverter Reduction
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Low power clock tree optimization method is proposed for clock buffer/inverter reduction. Redundant clock buffer can be found and deleted by “driving redundant” check and timing check. In inverter tree, four types of clock structure are discussed and method is proposed to find and delete redundant clock inverters for “1-to-1” structure and “1-to-n” structure. Test results show 7.7%-39% improve on buffer tree and 6.5%-21% improve on inverter tree.

articleTitle: A 160-nA 0.00039%/V All-MOSFET Voltage Reference With PSRR Superior Than -80 dB up to 1 GHz
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents an all-MOSFET voltage reference with relatively low power, high power supply ripple rejection (PSRR) and low line regulation (LR), which is designed in a standard 0.18-μm CMOS process. The proposed reference circuit consists of a proportional-to-absolute-temperature (PTAT) current generator and a reference voltage generator. Simultaneously, two low-pass filters built only by MOSFETs have been added to the circuit not only to enhance the PSRR but also to improve the LR without increasing much active area and supply current. Post-layout simulation results show the proposed voltage reference consumes a quiescent current around 160 nA when supply voltage is 1.7 V at room temperature. The PSRR is as high as -128 dB at low frequency, and better than -80 dB over the full frequency range. Besides, when supply voltage varies from 1.7 V to 3.8 V, a line regulation as low as 0.00039%/V is achieved. Moreover, the reference obtains a temperature coefficient (TC) of 21 ppm/°C when temperature varies from -40°C to 85°C. Owing to the fully-MOS structure, the total area of the proposed circuit is only around 0.014 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: A 14-18GHz 6bit passive phase shifter in 0.13µm SiGe BiCMOS
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A 6-bit digital switch-type passive phase shifter (PS) with low gain-variation is presented for satellite communication and Ku-band phased array radar. Switch-type high-pass/low-pass and bridged T-type topology are used to implement the 90°/180° and 5.625°/11.25°/22.5°/45° phase shifting cell, respectively. The PS is fabricated in 0.13µm BiCMOS (IBM 8HP) process. Measured results show that the PS achieves 4.2°-6° RMS phase error, and 0.3-0.6dB RMS gain error at 14–18 GHz. The total chip size is 2.7 x 1.1 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> with 0 mW DC power consumption.

articleTitle: Time Series Sequences Classification with Inception and LSTM Module
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Convolutional neural networks use parameter sharing to greatly reduce the number of weights. However, multi-channel feature maps greatly increase the amount of computation, and at the same time, it is difficult to continue to reduce the number of weights. The Inception module solves this problem by using global average pooling and network in network(NIN) architecture. We propose a deep neural network using the inception module and the LSTM module, using the inception module to reduce the computational complexity of the convolutional network, and using LSTM to preserve the internal timing characteristics of the time series dataset. At the same time, the sliding window method is used to simply augment the training data. The method was tested on the UCR time series classification archive, with a lower error rate than the baseline model.

articleTitle: A Switched-Capacitor DC-DC Converter with Unequal Duty Cycle for Ripple Reduction and Efficiency Improvement
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This work applies unequal duty cycle to switched-capacitor (SC) dc-dc converters to improve its output ripple as well as the power conversion efficiency. By adjusting the duty cycle, the charge and discharge states of the capacitor are reasonably balanced. Therefore, the output ripple is effectively reduced, and the charge redistribution loss is reduced, improving the efficiency. This scheme is verified with an SC converter with voltage conversion ratios (VCRs) of 1/4 and 1/3, and is simulated in a 65nm low-power process. Operating with a 33MHz switching frequency, an input voltage of 2.4V, an output range of 0.5~25mA, and a VCR of 1/4, the peak efficiency is increased by 1.0% and the output ripple is reduced by 43.6% compared to the equal duty cycle mode.

articleTitle: A Novel Low Channel Resistance LDMOS with Planar and Trench Gates
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A novel low channel resistance Lateral Double-diffusion Metal-Oxide Semiconductor (LDMOS) device with planar and trench gates is proposed and numerical simulated in this paper. The drift region of the device is based on the triple Reduced SURface Field (RESURF) and OPTimum Variational Lateral Doping (OPT-VLD) techniques, and the gate structure is improved to dual gates with a planar and a trench gates. The simulation results show that the gate channel resistance Rch and the specific on-resistance Ron,sp are reduced by more than 52.92% and 10.45%, respectively, in comparison with the conventional planar-gate triple RESURF OPT-VLD LDMOS device.

articleTitle: Digital Battery Management Unit with Built-In Resistance Compensation and Accidental Mutation Protection for Fast and Accurate Charging
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper proposes a digital battery management unit (BMU) with built-in resistance (BIR) compensation and accidental mutation protection (AMP) techniques to achieve fast and accurate charging, which applied in LDO-based charger. The digital compensation dynamically estimates the BIR. The battery can get fully charged with large rated charging current in pulsed constant current (PCC) mode and effectively reduced the charging time. AMP calibrates the mutate messages automatically to deal with some unexpected situations and guarantee the steady operation for the compensation module. The BMU is fabricated in 28 nm CMOS, occupies 0.014 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> of silicon area. Experimental results show that 73.3% charging time is reduced with 1.5A charging current. The power consumption of the digital chip is 59.1 μW.

articleTitle: A Small Wireless Power Transfer System for the Capsule Endoscopy
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: In order to solve the problem of energy limitation in capsule endoscopy, the button battery can be replaced by an external wireless power. A small wireless power transfer system for delivering power to capsule endoscopy has been presented here. The wireless power transfer system is built by using a small cylindrical receiving resonator and two cylindrical source resonators to transfer power through coupled magnetic resonance. Experimentally, it is found that the wireless power transfer efficiency is stable within a certain range due to the stable magnetic field generated by two source resonators. The proposed design has the significant advantage of stable power transfer and small size for capsule endoscopy.

articleTitle: A Front-End Integrated Circuit Design for Tactile Sensors
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a miniature front-end integrated circuit for tactile sensors. To achieve high sensing accuracy and density, a fast capacitance-to-voltage conversion module and an area efficient ADC module with high resolution is designed. The front-end IC is implemented based on SMIC 0.18μm CMOS process technology. Simulation results show that the conversion time of the C- V converter is 1.6 μs and the input range for the circuit is from 1 pF to 4pF. The proposed single-slope ADC has a 12-bit resolution and operates at 340-MHz clock frequency, with a differential nonlinearity of -0.09/+0.02 LSB and the integral nonlinearity of -0.68/+0.26 LSB. The proposed front-end IC shows the feasibility for the miniature tactile sensors.

articleTitle: The Design of a High-Efficiency Mode-Switching Power Amplifier With a Parallel Combining Transformer for LTE Application
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A 2.535 GHz mode-switching power amplifier (MSPA) for LTE (Long Term Evolution) application is presented in 65 nm CMOS process. By using self-biased technology and charge-acceleration-technique in the cascode structure, power-added efficiency (PAE) is increased. A center-tapped parallel combining transformer (PCT) is designed for power combining, which also provides a path for the second-order harmonic shorted ground. The passive efficiency of the transformer maintains above 80% from 2 GHz-3.5 GHz. The output 1-dB compressed power (P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1dB</sub>) and saturated output power (P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">SAT</sub>) are 23.69 dBm and 28 dBm. The peak PAE of the PA achieved 54.6%. With supply modulator (SM) is employed to improve PAE when the power is back off, the PA delivers 23.4 dBm LTE20 signal with 36.5% PAE.

articleTitle: An Improved Markov Model for Impulsive Noise over Automotive Power Line Communication Network
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Impulsive noise can have a great influence on the performance of in-vehicle power line communication systems. This paper presents an improved Markov chain model for impulsive noise modeling which can effectively reproduce the bursty nature of impulses. The proposed model is based on statistical analysis of the long-term measurements from the in-vehicle power distribution networks. First, the statistical properties regarding all impulse parameters, namely amplitude, duration, interval time and symbol, are explored. Then, four transition probability matrices based on Markov chain model are established. Finally, a process of reconstructing the impulsive noise with the four transition matrices is developed. Experiment results show that the proposed model is well suited for the description and modeling of the time and spectral behavior of impulsive noise.

articleTitle: A Dual-Channel Digital Low Dropout Regulator with Time-Division-Multiplexing Scheme
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A novel digital low dropout regulator (DLDO) that can simultaneously regulate two output channels with a shared controller is proposed in this paper. The time-division-multiplexing (TDM) scheme has been applied to the shared controller of this TDM DLDO and the total chip area is significantly reduced. Implemented in 130 nm CMOS process, the proposed TDM DLDO shows undershoot voltages of 68 mV and 85 mV at two output channels and only occupies a total chip area of 0.041 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, which is 40% less than the chip area of two independent DLDOs.

articleTitle: An Intelligent Surveillance System Based on Lightweight Object Detection Network L-SSD
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper proposes an intelligent surveillance system(ISS) based on Lightweight Single Shot Multibox Detector(L-SSD). L-SSD simplifies the backbone of SSD, dramatically reducing the cost of network computation by 28x fewer parameters than SSD. Furthermore, L-SSD adopts a novel method which can perform cross-layer feature fusion without increasing of computational resources. Firstly we implement L-SSD network on GPU and gets the performance of 6.5mAP at 65 fps for the VOC 2007 detection task. Then when L-SSD is actually implemented on NCS, its real-time frame rate can reach 7–8 fps.

articleTitle: A High Phase Accuracy Multiphase DLL with Optimized VCDL Structure
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: In this paper, a 4-phase delay-locked loop (DLL) with high phase accuracy, low power consumption and small area is realized for time-to-digital converter (TDC). The proposed DLL adopts a new voltage-controlled delay line (VCDL) structure, which reduces the output phase error down to 2.32%. A simple digital auxiliary pulse width regulator is used to adjust the width of output pulse for further reduction of the duty cycle error. Designed with 0.18 μm CMOS process, the DLL with 4-phase outputs occupies an active area of 102 μm × 100 μm. With a supply voltage of 1.8 V, the power and peak-to-peak jitter of this proposed DLL is 2.27 mW and 12.9 ps, respectively.

articleTitle: Effect of Trench Bottom Implantation on the Performance of Trench MOSFET
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A trench MOSFET with trench bottom implantation (TBI) is formed to improve the device performance and reliability. Devices with various TBI conductivity types are studied by numerical simulations in this paper. The N-channel trench MOSFETs with P-TBI region and N-TBI region are compared in the aspect of static and dynamical characteristics. It is found that N-MOSFET with P-TBI region alleviates the electric field of the bottom oxide at the off-state, and achieves a higher breakdown voltage than that with N-type TBI region due to space charge compensation. However, P-type TBI region narrows the current path and causes on-resistance degradation. Besides, when the device is turned on, P-type TBI region stores negative charge and results in higher electric field.

articleTitle: Analysis and Design of Milimeter-Wave Neutralized Power Amplifiers in 65-nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents two single-stage common-source differential power amplifiers (PAs) at 28 GHz. One PA utilizes the metal-oxide-metal (MOM) capacitor neutralization topology and the other adopts the NMOS transistor capacitor neutralization. The input and output matching networks of the two PAs are both implemented by transformers, which are carefully optimized to enhance high load capacity and efficiency. Fabricated in 65-nm CMOS technology, the PA with MOM capacitor neutralization shows a measured small-signal gain of 7.05 dB and a peak power added efficiency (PAE) of 27.52%. The PA with NMOS neutralization achieves a small-signal gain of 6.17 dB with a peak PAE of 25.54%. By comparison under the same DC consumption, the latter presents higher stability and broader bandwidth at the cost of gain and efficiency.

articleTitle: Convolutional Neural Network Accelerator on FPGA
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents the design and FPGA implementation of a convolutional neural network accelerator (CNNA). Two kinds of sparsity, zero-valued weights and zero-valued input feature map, are exploited to save power. The design features hierarchical memory organization to reduce external memory access. Bandwidth compression and decompression are also proposed to reduce external memory bandwidth. The unified scratch memory can be configured dynamically layer-by-layer to maximize memory utilization. The proposed CNNA is designed in Xilinx high level synthesis (HLS) language and implemented on ZCU102 board. With totally 2048 multiply-and-accumulation (MAC) unit, the design is able to deliver 1TOPS computing power when running at 250MHz.

articleTitle: Low-power, High Speed and High Uniform Switching in AIOx-based Memristor using Homogeneous Bilayer Structure for Memcomputing
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: High-performance memristor is greatly desired to develop memcomputing. Here, we report a W/AlO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>/Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>/Pt memristor based on oxygen vacancy filament engineering. The oxygen-rich AlO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub> film fabricated by sputtering (RF) severs as oxygen vacancy (Vo) reservoir with low oxygen chemical potential and high mobility, whereas the denser AI<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>film deposited by atomic layer deposition (ALD) acts as a dominant resistive switching (RS) layer. Our device, which satisfies promising characteristics for data storage and memcomputing, displays low-power, high-uniformity, large on/off ratio, high-speed and high-temperature stability at 125 °C.

articleTitle: Chip-Area-Efficient Capacitor-less LDO Regulator with Fast-Transient Response
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: In this paper, a fully-on-chip, NMOS low dropout voltage (LDO) regulator with a capacitance multiplier used for improving the stability and transient response is proposed. This compensation technology emulates a large capacitance value at the gate of the pass FET for high stability and fast transient response. The chip area is much reduced compared to a conventional design. The proposed LDO is designed in a 0.18-μm CMOS process and consumes 13.2 μA quiescent current with 0.1 V dropout and 1.0 V output voltages. It does not require any external compensation capacitor.

articleTitle: A Hardware System for Fast AER Object Classification with On-chip Online Learning
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper proposes a customized VLSI system for fast address-event representation (AER) object classification based on simple random ferns. The system architecture maximizes data throughput by employing circuit pipelines, while minimizing chip resource cost by allowing the datapath to be dynamically reused for both class inference and online learning procedures. The extra time consumed for learning on the chip is negligible. An FPGA prototype of the proposed system was implemented. It can process up to 100 million AER spikes per second and achieves 77.2% classification accuracy on the MNIST-DVS dataset.

articleTitle: A Reconfigurable Cache Structure Design for Multi-core SOC
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Cache is a common method for mitigating the difference in data bandwidth between chip and external memory. This paper proposes a shared storage structure for a heterogeneous multi-core SOC system face to high-density calculation. The storage architecture uses a reconfigurable design approach which uses a part of the secondary shared cache as a local private store of the FFT compute node. This structure takes into account resource consumption and computational efficiency, and can save a large amount of on-chip storage resources compared to the common secondary shared cache. Compared with the cache-free structure, this structure can provide up to 41.1% acceleration ratio.

articleTitle: Ultra-low Power Relaxation Oscillator Based on Negative Capacitance Ferroelectric Field-Effect Transistor
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel Ferroelectric Field-Effect transistor (FeFET) based relaxation oscillator. The novel relaxation oscillator circuit utilizes proposed biasing circuit and unique characteristics of FeFET including negative capacitance (NC), very low subthreshold swing, high transconductance (g<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf>) and high channel conductance, to achieve ultra-low power and fast start up. Circuit simulation results show that the proposed NC-FeFET based oscillator at 0.6 V in 0.18 µm technology has achieved 88.7% lower power and 81.6% shorter start-up time, than the CMOS-based counterpart.

articleTitle: 28-GHz band Omnidirectional Lens Antenna for Channel Measurements
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a novel lens antenna to achieve high and stable omnidirectional gain working at 28-GHz band for 5G millimeter-wave channel measurement applications. The proposed antenna consists of an annular extended hemispherical lens and a small stepped biconical antenna as the feed source, which makes the antenna wide in bandwidth, high and stable in omnidirectional gain. The designed antenna can achieve a -10-dB impedance bandwidth of 22.2% with stable vertical polarized omnidirectional radiation pattern in range of 24 to 30 GHz. The omnidirectional gain is up to 11dBi at 27 GHz, and the rotationally symmetrical structure and feeding ensure good omnidirectional gain stability.

articleTitle: A 10b 50 MS/s single-Channel asynchronous SAR ADC with two alternate comparators and comparator calibration
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A 10b 50 MS/s successive approximation register (SAR) ADC based on TSMC 0.18 um is implemented. A redundant capacitor DAC is applied to improve the accuracy of the comparator. Each sample is converted by using alternate comparators with two edge synchronous asynchronous clocks for high speed and low kickback noise. And the foreground calibration and background calibration based on the comparator offset of this structure are proposed.

articleTitle: A 343.2-348.9 GHz CMOS Terahertz Source with On-Chip Antennas
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a terahertz source using standard CMOS process. The terahertz source is implemented with 4 mutual coupling oscillator cores based on injection locking theory. The push-push architecture is adopted in each oscillator core to generate the fourth harmonic signal. Moreover, on-chip patch antenna is integrated with each oscillator to radiate the output power. Frequency tuning is achieved by changing the phase shift between adjacent oscillators. The simulation results show that the source operates at the fundamental frequency of 86.5 GHz. The simulated fourth harmonic output power of each core is -15 dBm and the phase noise is -115 dBc/Hz at 10 MHz offset.

articleTitle: A Ku-band CMOS 6-bit Digital-Controlled Phase-Invariant Variable Gain Amplifier and Attenuator
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a 6-bit CMOS digital-controlled gain-tuning building block in phased array. The proposed building block combines a 15-dB-tuning phase-invariant variable gain amplifier (VGA) with a 15-dB-tuning attenuator (ATT). Thus, 30-dB tuning range and 0.5-dB resolution with <; 4.6° RMS phase variation are achieved in the designed frequency range (10.5 GHz-13 GHz).

articleTitle: An Efficient and Low-Overhead Chip-to-Chip Interconnect Protocol Design for NOC
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: As the scale of the multicore system expands, it may extend to multiple chips with chip-to-chip interconnect, and its data transmission needs to be fast and efficient. Network on chips (NOCs) has become the mainstream structure for distributed multicore connections, while there are few inter-chip protocols for NOC. In this paper, a highly efficient and low-overhead chip-to-chip interconnect protocol design for NOC is proposed, which consists of data link layer, physical layer and flow control mechanism design. By using ZCU102 evaluation kit, we validate our protocol design with various dataflow, achieving up to 10 Gb/s/lane line rate.

articleTitle: A 30-V Floating Level Shifter with Sub-700-ps Delay and Sub-300-ps Edge Time for GaN Driver
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: In this paper, a high-voltage high-speed floating voltage level shifter with sub-nanosecond delay used for half-bridge GaN driver is proposed. The proposed level shifter is based on the cross-coupled structure. By eliminating a high-impedance node and introducing a pull-up module, the voltage transition can be sped up. The proposed level shifter is designed in 0.18-μm CMOS technology, and the simulation results show it can work with maximum 30-V supply voltage. A conduction delay of 681.4 ps and a turn-off delay of 519.9 ps are achieved respectively. The rising and falling time are 295 ps and 178 ps, respectively.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Floating-tap Decision Feedback Equalizer for a 2.5 to 10 Gbps Receiver
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: An adaptive decision feedback equalizer (DFE) with floating tap architecture is proposed. An eye height detector is designed to perform the number selection of the DFE taps. An optimized sign-sign least mean square (SSLMS) algorithm is developed to automatically update the coefficients of the DFE taps. Based on a 55 nm CMOS process, a receiver with an operation range of 2.5 to 10 Gbps is designed. The simulation results show that the DFE is able to provide an 8-17 dB compensation ability, and the power consumption is 10.9 mW at 10 Gbps.

articleTitle: A 10 Gb/s, 150 mA Laser Diode Driver with Active Back-Termination in 0.13-µm SOI CMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: The design of a 10 Gb/s laser diode driver (LDD) in 0.13-μm SOI CMOS technology is described. The driver utilizes cross-coupled neutralization capacitors and integrates a tunable negative capacitance circuit to extend the bandwidth. Loading reflections due to the imperfect matching at the laser side are absorbed by an active back termination (ABT) circuit. Compared to a driver with a resistive termination, the proposed driver reduces the power dissipation by 40%. The LDD can deliver a modulation current ranges from 10 to 150 mA to 25-Ω lasers with a preserved dynamic performance due to the usage of a segmented output driver scheme. Post-layout simulation results show that the proposed driver has a bandwidth of 7 GHz, and the return loss is better than 8.6 dB in the frequency band of interest. The driver supports DC and AC coupling to 25-Ω lasers with a total power dissipation of 1.06 and 0.72 W, respectively at maximum output current. The physical layout occupies an area of 0.84 × 0.9 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Microstrip/SAW-Resonator Wideband Bandpass Filter
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: In this paper, a hybrid microstrip/SAW-resonator wideband bandpass filter by combining microstrip-lines and SAW resonators is reported. It is based on transversal filtering section that are shaped by a parallel connection of a SAW resonator and a transmission-line. With the proposed filter topology, a passband with enhanced fractional FBW (i.e., larger than the electromechanical coupling coefficient Kt<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> of its constituent SAW resonator) can be achieved. The wideband filtering function of the filter is presented by selecting a high Kt<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> SAW resonator. Through simulation analysis, the filter with a 2.3GHz SAW resonator exhibits a FBW of 10.35%.

articleTitle: A 112-Gb/s PAM-4 T/2-spaced 5-Tap FFE in 0.13-µm BiCMOS
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A 5-tap T/2-spaced 112-Gb/s Feed-Forward Equalizer (FFE) with four-level pulse-amplitude modulation (PAM-4) in a 0.13-µm BiCMOS process is presented. A number of bandwidth enhancement techniques are used, which allow high-speed operation while consuming 113.2 mW from a 1.8-V supply. The gain ripple of each delay tap is less than 1 dB up to 28 GHz to ensure low jitter. In addition, a 3-tap T-spaced 112-Gb/sPAM-4 FFE is designed and compared with this work to showcase the pronounced advantage of T/2-spaced FFE in PAM-4 equalization.

articleTitle: Application of Ultrathin Organic Insulating Films for Electronic Package
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A insulation layer can provide separation between the different electrical signals in electronic package. Herein, poly(methacrylimide) (PMI) and poly(methylacrylic acid) (PMAA) initiate by 4-Nitrobenzene diazonium (NBD) tetrafluoroborate are grafted on 4-inch silicon wafer. O2 plasma is applied to improve adhesion property. Peeling experiment shows the treatment exhibited a better adhesion property with metals than no plasma treatment. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is used to determine the position of adhesion break point and analyze changes in surface composition. The mechanism of effect of O2 plasma is discussed. Nanostructure and surface composition are supposed the key point of plasma modification mechanism.

articleTitle: A Fully-Integrated Kinetic Energy Harvesting Circuit with a Transposed Hybrid Series-Parallel SC DC-DC
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A fully integrated piezoelectric kinetic energy harvesting circuit is presented, in which the active rectifier adopts 5-T amplifiers instead of high-gain comparators to reduce the power loss at very low tapping frequencies. For the on-chip switched-capacitor DC-DC, a transposed hybrid series-parallel structure is proposed to reduce the number of capacitors and switches remarkably, resulting in small chip area and high efficiency. Fabricated in a 0.18-μm CMOS process with a die size of 0.748 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, the peak output power is 121.8 μW at about 2 Hz frequency manual tapping on the piezoelectric transducer.

articleTitle: Fast Determination of the Potential for Cu Superfilling Using a Nanoporous Electrode
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Due to the specific geometry of through silicon vias, the optimization of additives' concentrations used in Cu deposition often meets difficulty when using a normal flat surface as the working electrode. In this work, a nanoporous structured electrode and a flat electrode were employed to mimic the entire via and the via top, respectively. The difference in current between the two electrodes represented the current contribution of the via bottom. Hence, a simple method that comparing the current of via top and via bottom was proposed for the determination of the applied potential and was proved to be be applicable to the actual feature filling.

articleTitle: An Attention Pooling based Channel Accumulation for Target Classification of Harmonic Radar
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper proposes an attention pooling method based on channel accumulation of spectrograms for harmonic radar target classification. The traditional method of audio recognition is feeding the two-dimensional (2D) spectrograms directly into the 2D Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), which does not extract depth detail features and just has a low recognition accuracy for the spectrograms with little differences. To address the issues, we propose an attention pooling for the recognition. It uses multiple one-dimensional (1D) convolution layers to accumulate data in a certain dimension (time or frequency) of 2D spectrograms. Then we get the 1D feature accumulation maps and train them with 1D CNN classifier. The experiments show that the 1D CNN with attention pooling based channel accumulation achieved 90.88% average accuracy, while the traditional 2D CNN is 78.97%. The former is 11.91% higher recognition accuracy than the latter, which can be applied to harmonic radar target classification.

articleTitle: A Low Phase Noise Injection-Locked Ring PLL Based a Sub-Sampling Loop
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: In this paper, an injection-locked phase-locked loop (ILPLL) based a sub-sampling loop (SSL) with low phase noise and low jitter is presented. A sub-sampling loop is used to subsample the ring VCO output with the injection pulse. The SSL is used to detect the phase difference of the output differential pair of the RVCO and generate a control signal to realign the phase of the differential output pair of the RVCO. Therefore, the center of the injection pulse can be made to occur at the zero crossing of the RVCO output by constant adjustment. A 200MHz PLL is developed by use of 55nm CMOS technology. The phase noise is -132 dBc/Hz at 1MHz offsets.

articleTitle: A Low-Power Digital Control Core with High-Speed SPI Slave for Phased Array Application in 40nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A low-power digital control circuit with high-speed serial peripheral interface (SPI) is presented in this paper, which enables fast and flexible configuration of integrated multi-channel phased arrays. The addressable digital control circuit enables amplitude, phase and other control registers configuration. The SPI enables full-duplex, one-to-many and high-speed communication between the master and slaves. In addition, if a transmission error occurs, it will be detected and reported by internal error mechanisms. The proposed circuit has been fabricated and tested in 40nm CMOS. The measurement results show that this digital circuit can stably work at a clock rate of 100 MHz with 0.1 mW power consumption and 0.036 mm2 silicon area overhead. The high-speed and low-power digital circuit is expected to be widely used in the future integrated multi-channel phased array designs.

articleTitle: Study of Thickness-Dependent Mobility of MoS2FETs with HfO2 Encapsulation by Edge Contact
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Back-gate molybdenum disulfide (MoS<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>) field effect transistors (FETs) are very sensitive to thickness of channel material because of weak dielectric screening and strong interlayer coupling in multilayer Mos<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>. In this paper, we utilize soft Argon (Ar) plasma to pattern Mos<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> to make edge contact to Mos<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>. Then, the Mos<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> flake on SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>/Si substrate is coated with 30 nm HfO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> using ALD to get the Hfo<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>/MoS<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>/SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> heterostructure. Experimental results show that the carrier mobility of 9 nm Mos<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> back gate FET is up to 38 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/(V*s) at room temperature.

articleTitle: A 2.4-to-4 GHz VCO Achieving -137dB c/Hz Phase Noise at 1MHz Offset in 28 nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a low noise NMOS-only LC-VCO. A tail inductor and a center-tapped spiral inductor are utilized to suppress noise. A wide tuning range is achieved with the help of a switched capacitor bank. Based on the post-layout simulation results, the VCO exhibits a wide turning range from 2.4GHz to 4GHz, and a low phase noise from -132dBc/Hz to -137dBc/Hz at 1MHz frequency offset over the whole operating frequency, which is 10dB better than the conventional VCOs without tail inductor. It consumes minimum 42.8mW and maximum 58.6mW from a 1.8V supply and the VCO core occupies 0.15mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> total area in 28nm CMOS process technology.

articleTitle: Real-Time Arbitrary Style Transfer with Convolution Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Style transfer is a research hotspot in computer vision. Up to now, it is still a challenge although many researches have been conducted on it for high quality style transfer. In this work, we propose an algorithm named ASTCNN which is a real-time Arbitrary Style Transfer Convolution Neural Network. The ASTCNN consists of two independent encoders and a decoder. The encoders respectively extract style and content features from style and content and the decoder generates the style transferred image images. Experimental results show that ASTCNN achieves higher quality output image than the state-of-the-art style transfer algorithms and the floating point computation of ASTCNN is 23.3% less than theirs.

articleTitle: Digital-to-Time Converter Gain Calibration with a Muxed Delay Locked Loop
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Digital-to-time converters (DTC) have found increasing adoption in frac-N PLLs to compensate for the excess phase error caused by delta-sigma modulator (DSM). DTC gain has to be calibrated in order to achieve the intended compensation. Existing digital DTC calibration methods require various forms of time to digital conversion (TDC). In this paper a low complexity and area efficient analog DTC calibration method without the need for a TDC is proposed. It is based on a delay locked loop with an input-muxed phase frequency detector (PFD). The input clock signals to the PFD are muxed by the sign of the excess phase error from the DSM. This analog calibration method is functionally equivalent to the conventional sign-error Least Mean Square calibration methods implemented in digital domain. Circuit non-idealities including noise and phase offset can be mitigated. DTC gain calibration error <; 1% can be achieved in mixed-signal simulation.

articleTitle: Improvement of read disturb on TaOx-based RRAM cells with optimized pulse programming method
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: In this work, we proposed a reset pulse operation programming using multiple pulses with small width, which greatly improved the read disturb of the TaO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>-based RRAM device. The robust read disturb was also observed after the devices baked at 90°C, 120°C and 150°C respectively. These results indicate that the proposed pulse optimization method improves the robustness of read disturb. The improvement can be attributed to the reduced energy consumed in the whole reset process.

articleTitle: Mechanical properties of the low-k material measured by tensile tests
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Low-k materials are widely used in the IC (Integrate Circuit) integration, which weaken mechanical properties are critical in packaging reliability designs. In this study, the thin film of low-k material was fabricated, patterned and marked by the tiny ink dots for measuring its mechanical properties by uniaxial tensile tests. The method improves test accuracy by avoiding errors from samples ends and clamps in tensile test. The Young's module, Poisson's ratio and fracture toughness of the low-k material are obtained by the method.

articleTitle: A Highly Linear 25–32 GHz Power Amplifier with 22-dBm Output Power and 30% PAE in 130-nm SiGe BiCMOS
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: In this paper, a two-stage, two-way transformer combined power amplifier (PA) operated in 25–32 GHz frequency range in 130-nm SiGe BiCMOS technology is proposed. We propose the output cell parameters optimization targeting high gain, OP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1dB</inf>, and PAE for SiGe BiCMOS HBT. Based on the derived transformer model and graphical matching procedure, we present an optimization methodology to design low loss output, inter-stage and input transformers. The inductive source degeneration is utilized to broaden impedance matching bandwidth. Measurement results show that the proposed PA achieves 26 dB gain, 1-dB compressed output power of 22.1-dBm and 30% power-added efficiency (PAE) at 1-dB compression point.

articleTitle: Research of Noise Suppression on Source Follower in TDI Image Sensor
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: In order to promote the applications of image sensor in space observation, 1/f noise from SF (Source Follower) in TDI (Time Delay and Integration) image sensor need to further improve. Three types of SFs are tested, including Nvt (native voltage threshold), Lvt (low voltage threshold) and normal SF. They are designed in different size to verify the optimal design additionally. Comparing the data, Nvt and Lvt SF perform better than normal SF versus noise and Cvg. In small size, less than 1/1μm, Lvt and Nvt SF are on the same level. In large size, greater than 1/1μm, Nvt SF performs better.

articleTitle: Enhanced FIR-embedded noise reduction method with hybrid phase detection for semidigital fractional-N phase-locked loops
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper describes a phase noise reduction method with hybrid phase detection in the design of semidigital ΔΣ phase-locked loops (PLLs) that employ a finite impulse response (FIR) filtering technique for quantization noise reduction. A static phase offset problem is addressed and the use of a hybrid phase detector is proposed to further enhance noise and spur reduction performance. It is also shown that the FIR filtering not only suppresses out-of-band quantization noise but also improves in-band noise by mitigating the nonlinearity effect of the charge pump. Behavior simulation results show that the proposed semidigital ΔΣ PLL improves the in-band noise and reference spur performance by 20dB compared with the conventional ΔΣ PLL.

articleTitle: A Spike-Based Background Light Suppression Time-of-Flight Pixel for Outdoor Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: In this paper, a spike-based background light suppression ToF pixel is proposed. This pixel adopts a novel in-pixel background light suppression circuit. The in-pixel background light suppression circuit can realize effective self-suppression of the background light and convert the received infrared light intensity to the number of spikes. The proposed ToF pixel is designed in a 0.11μm CMOS image sensor technology with a physical size of 27.5 × 27.5μm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Simulation results illustrate that the proposed pixel is capable of suppressing background light of 30dB BRS without filter. The ToF sensor with the proposed pixel can not only used in indoor applications but also used in high intensity background applications.

articleTitle: A 143.4-151.5 GHz High DC-RF Efficiency Signal Source in 65nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a 143.4-151.5 GHz high DC-RF efficiency signal source. Using the proposed mutual inductance cancelling technique, 1) the fundamental signal generated by the V-band oscillator is fed to the varactors, 2) the second harmonic signal generated by the varactors is prevented from flowing back to the V-band oscillator, and is all fed to the output buffer instead. With post-simulated results using 65 nm CMOS technology, the signal source shows an output power of -0.65 dBm, a DC-RF efficiency of 4.0% and a tuning range of 5.5%. The signal source consumes 21.53 mW using a 1.2 V voltage supply. The whole die area including the pads is 0.075 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Parasitic Parameters Extraction for PD SOI MOSFETs Using Four-Port Network
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: In this work, four-port network structure was used into small signal parameters extraction for radio frequency (RF) metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistors (MOSFETs) in partially depleted (PD) silicon-on-insulator (SOI) technology. Small signal scanting parameters (S-parameters) for N-type T-gate (TB) MOSFETs were measured from 0.1 GHz to 30.1 GHz through GSGSG probes. A simple model topology of four-port network was analyzed and small signal parasitic resistance and capacitance are extracted from conductance parameters and impedance parameters converted from S-parameters.

articleTitle: High-Mobility Polymer Monolayer Field-Effect Transistors with Graphene Electrodes
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Polymer monolayer field-effect transistors provide an excellent platform to investigate the charge transport mechanism, however, most studies only reported the mobility of ≤ 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup>cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup> V<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>. This study select the graphene as electrode materials, significantly improving the morphology of polymer monolayer at the edge of the electrodes. As a result, a maximum saturated mobility of 0.73 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup> V<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>is obtained. Additionally, the channel length is found to have minor effect on the charge transport ranging from 20 to 100 μm.

articleTitle: Based on 1 or 0 BNN Accelerator with Array Architecture
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: In this paper, we introduce a binary convolutional neural network accelerator which using a new binarization method. We propose the weights and the activations to either 1 or 0 instead of +1 or -1, which makes the convolution process simplified and more suitable for hardware implementation. To decrease the data access from off-chip memory, we propose a novel method of the data reuse, which can reduce 58.8% data access. Our accelerator is implemented on the VC709 Evaluation Kit. Experimental results show that the proposed accelerator achieves a throughput of 3378 GOPS and 1624 GOPS/W energy efficiency.

articleTitle: On-Chip High-Voltage Buffer Design for Implantable Neural/Muscular Stimulators
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents an on-chip buffer design for implantable high-voltage neural/muscle stimulators. The buffer is designed in 0.18 μm CMOS process technology with 24-V LDMOS option. The output voltage of the buffer can reach 10 V and the static power consumption is 81 μW. The load regulation of this 10-V buffer is 0.07% for sinking load current and 0.09% for sourcing load current. The simulation result shows the designed on-chip high-voltage buffer can be integrated and used in the neural/muscular stimulation system.

articleTitle: Quad-band Balun Filter using Dual-mode Spiral Slotline Notched Structure with Enhanced Selectivity
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A quad-band balun bandpass filter (BPF) based on dual-mode notched-band structure is presented in this paper. The proposed notched structure is composed of two spiral slotline stubs (SSSs) loaded along the main slotline path. Each SSSs pair introduces two transmission zeroes (TZs) with enhanced roll-off skirt selectivity. By utilizing microstrip and SSSs structures on both side of the substrate respectively, the proposed balun BPF achieves competitive selectivity over four operating passbands, as well as good balance performance. Moreover, the harmonics of introduced multiple TZ pairs help to suppress high frequency resonance, resulting in a wide stopband. A prototype quad-band balun BPF operating at 1.6, 2.5, 3.5 and 5.3 GHz is fabricated and measured results demonstrate an amplitude imbalance of less than 0.45 dB and a phase imbalance of less than 5.1°.

articleTitle: A 100Gb/s PAM-4 Receiver Analog Front-End
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper describes an inverter-based receiver analog front-end design using T-coil technique implemented in a 40nm CMOS process. The proposed T-coil can separate the capacitance of PAD and preamplifier itself, to achieve a total bandwidth enhancement ratio of 2.7. The proposed continuous time linear equalizer(CTLE) adopts a negative feedback loop to generate low frequency zero-pole pair to slower down the compensation slope. The simulation result shows that the transimpedance gain of the system is 76.5 dBΩ under the bandwidth of 37GHz. The input referred noise current in maximum gain mode is 2.3uArms.

articleTitle: A Light-Weight Feasible Region Detection Method in Autonomous Walking Intelligent Robots
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: It is crucial to ensure the reliability and safety for intelligent robots. The premise of ensuring security is how to effectively perceive the external environment and extract the feasible region. In this paper, a light-weight feasible region detection method is proposed, which extracts the rough feasible region based on three-component information in Hue, Saturation, Value (HSV) space and then perfects the feasible region through edge extraction. The experimental results show that our method can achieve effective performance in the movement of intelligent robots.

articleTitle: A Robust Differential 4x28Gb/s Stacked Optical Receiver in 28nm CMOS Realizing Crosstalk Suppression and Power Supply Rejection
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A stacked 4×28Gb/s multi-channel optical receivers with good crosstalk and power supply noise suppression is presented in this paper. Each channel is consisted of a transimpedance amplifier (TIA), a two-stage level shifter (LS), a post amplifier (PA) and an output buffer (OB), realizing 66dBΩ transimpedance gain and 21GHz bandwidth. The receiver adopts P-type current-mode-logic (CML) pseudo-differential architecture, making it robust to power supply noise and crosstalk. The fully integrated power supply is comprised of a main LDO and three assist LDOs. The stacked receivers consume 58.9mW from 3.3V supply, in which the power supply regulator dissipates 2.3mW.

articleTitle: A Closed-loop Controlled Neural Stimulator with High Voltage Compliance in 0.18-µm Low Voltage CMOS Teachnology
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: An H-bridge based neural stimulator is designed and implemented in TSMC 0.18 µm 3.3V CMOS technology. It is mainly composed of dynamic charge pumps, high voltage interface units and a current source. The closed-loop controlled sub-system is presented to transfer the stimulator into a closed-loop system. To avoid the unwanted current spike that may cause in the conventional H-bridge working process, the additional work states are added. The simulation results show that the maximum stimulation voltage magnitude is up to 12.6V and the maximum stimulation current is 100µA.

articleTitle: Super steep SS “PN-Body tied SOI-FET” with 65 nm thin Box FD-SOI
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Characteristics of the super-steep subthreshold slope (SS) PN-body tied (PNBT) SOI-FET was confirmed with the 65 nm thin buried oxide (Box) fully depleted (FD)-SOI process, for the first time. The substrate bias (Vsub) was necessary for inducing the super-steep SS on 65 nm PNBT SOI-FETs. It is noted that the super-steep SS is observed with the negative and also the positive Vsub. The body current was below one tenth of the drain current. The trade-off between Ion/Ioff ratio and the hysteresis window was also shown. The confirmation of the super-steep SS PNBT SOI-FET on 65 nm technology is adding to confirmation on 200 nm SOI technology, so far, and is also valuable for ultralow power applications.

articleTitle: Analyzing Subharmonic Oscillation of Current-Mode Buck Converters with the Circuit-Oriented Geometrical Approach
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: In this paper, the circuit-oriented geometrical approach in predicting subharmonic oscillation (SHO) of voltage-mode switching converters has been exteneded to analyze SHO of current-mode buck converters. The critical conditions of the SHO of the current-mode controlled buck converters working in both continuous conduction mode (CCM) and discontinuous conduction mode (DCM) are systematically derived. It can be observed that SHO always occurs when the duty ratio is larger than 0.5 no matter how the current loop is designed, and can only be avoided by using ramp compenstaion technique. Moreover, the critical conditions in voltage-mode control in fact could be considered as a special case of those in current-mode control, and a unified critical condition for both control methods is derived. Cadence simulation results are presented to verify the analysis.

articleTitle: A 1mW, 1.6-6.4MHz Bandwidth, 21dB-Gain-Range Analog Baseband with >94dB SFDR
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A low power and high linearity merged analog baseband (MABB) with tunable bandwidth (BW) and programmable gain is proposed for multi-standard integrated wireless receivers in this paper. The MABB consists of an Active-RC low-pass filter and a programmable gain amplifier (PGA). An operational amplifier (op amp) for high gain-bandwidth (GBW) product under low supply voltage is proposed. A R-kR resistor ladder is used in the PGA to achieve a closed-loop gain independent of bandwidth and 3dB gain step. The proposed MABB covers a bandwidth range from 1.6MHz to 6.4MHz and the gain could be tuned from 6 to 27dB. The MABB, designed in 40nm CMOS, achieves >94 dB SFDR for 27dB gain and a 570-mV<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">pp-diff</sub> output signal amplitude, while consuming 1.147mW under a 0.9V supply voltage.

articleTitle: A Programmable Capacitance-to-Voltage Converter for MEMS Capacitive Sensors
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A Programmable Capacitance-to-voltage converter for MEMS capacitive sensors is proposed. The main circuit consists of balance capacitor arrays, capacitance transimpedance amplifier, sample/hold, low pass filter, and output buffer. Capacitance-to-voltage converter detects the change in capacitance between two capacitors and provides an output voltage proportional to it, with a capacitance resolution of 1.70 aF/√Hz at bandwidth of 500 Hz. The converter has advantages of tuning the gain, bandwidth, feedback capacitor, balance capacitor and output offset. It can be used as a general circuit for the application on a variety of MEMS capacitive sensors.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Parser for Software Defined Network L4 Ethernet Switch Chip
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: a reconfigurable packet parser suitable for an L4 Ethernet switch chip is proposed to satisfy the flexibility and versatility requirements of software defined network to hardware. It implements the basic fixed functions by fixed hardware while user-defined functions by reconfigurable logic in addition to programmable execution unit. Thus, it does not only enable users to define the protocols but also enables users to define the actions during parsing. Its highest packet throughput is 240M packets per-second. Its size is about 7.37 million gates.

articleTitle: A 320x240-pixel Sub-centimeter Resolution Time-of-Flight Image Sensor Design with Structure and Doping Optimized Pinned Photodiode Pixels
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A Pinned-Photodiode (PPD) indirect Time-of-Flight (ToF) sensor and circuits have been optimized and fabricated. Tailored to improve the demodulation contrast and quantum efficiency, pixel shape modification, step implantation improvement and pixel area optimization are applied. In the simulation, the results support the expectation of better performance. The sensor and related circuits are implemented based on TCAD and EDA tools. In measurement the tested results indicate that maximum modulation frequency is 54 MHz, the quantum efficiency is 19% and the measuring range is 0.5-6.5m with these techniques.

articleTitle: A 99.2 dB SNDR Feedforward Delta-Sigma Modulator with Build-In Summation Quantizer
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A new type of quantizer with build-in weighted summation function is proposed for replacing summer in feedforward delta sigma modulators. To verify the validity, a 2nd-order 8-level modulator based on this quantizer has been implemented in 180 nm CMOS technology. Simulation results show that the modulator achieves a 99.2 dB SNDR in 25 kHz bandwidth while consumes 1.56 mW under 1.8 V supply.

articleTitle: Design of Low Power Multiplier for Vision chips
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: With the popularity of pruning operations in neural networks, the percentage of zero-operands in mainstream neural network computing is getting higher. To meet the low-power requirements of neural network computing, the zero-skipping operation in multiplication is used in deep learning computing. This paper proposes a zero-skipping design of low-power multiplier for vision chips, which reduces the power consumption of the arithmetic and logic unit (ALU) by up to 32%, of which the low power consumption effect is remarkable.

articleTitle: A High-Accuracy Digital Low-Dropout Regulator with Limit Cycle Oscillation Reduction Technique
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: The digital low-dropout regulator is appropriate for the digital circuits for its low-voltage and low-power design. However, the digital LDOs suffer an output voltage ripple caused by the limit cycle oscillation and its accuracy needs to be improved. This paper presents a limit cycle oscillation reduction technique for the digital LDOs to suppress the output voltage ripple. The proposed technique uses a two-stage regulation method to add a fine MOSFETs array and a second-stage barrel shifter to the traditional digital LDOs. The simulation results show that the proposed technique reduces the output voltage ripple from 3.72 mV to 0.49 mV on the average and the regulation accuracy is improved about 8 times.

articleTitle: A Low-power H.265/HEVC 4K@30 Video Decoder with Dynamic Power Gating
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper describes the design of a low-power H.265/HEVC 4096×2160@30fps decoder with dynamic power gating. We show that as the shrinking of technology node and the increasing of leakage power, circuit operating under “just-enough” or baseline frequency may not be the best solution in terms of total power consumption. By introducing various operating modes and dynamic power gating of inactive part of the design, we evaluate the total power consumptions of a H.265/HEVC video decoding system under different frequencies for various resolutions. We proposed both theoretical calculation and post-layout simulation result under 65nm technology, showing that the optimum power point occurs at a higher frequency other than minimum. By choosing proper operating mode, we are able to achieve up to 38% power reduction with negligible hardware overhead and no performance degradation.

articleTitle: A review on Z2-FET and PISD based on Silicon-on-insulator substrate
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper reviews our recent work on two novel semiconductor devices built on silicon-on-insulator (SOI) substrate. The Z<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>-FET, which operates with feedback mechanism, has been demonstrated with extremely sharp switching behaviors and gate-controlled hysteresis. It has found applications in high performance memories, electrostatic discharge protection and photodetection. PISD utilizes the substrate of SOI for photon-electron conversion and senses the photoelectron in-situ without need of any additional device. It has been used as one-transistor active pixel sensor (1T-APS) which is more compact than conventional CMOS sensor.

articleTitle: An Analog-Memoryless Near Sensor Computing Architecture for Always-On Intelligent Perception Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: In always-on intelligent visual perception applications, Convolution Neural Network algorithm has been widely applied. However, the implementation of it's processing is limited by hardware resources and energy budgets, which come from data access, interface overhead and inflexible configuration. In this paper, we present a novel analog architecture that implements low-precision Binary Neural Network and fuses with CMOS image sensor for always-on applications. By enabling current-mode computation in analog domain, the overhead of analog-to-digital converter as well as analog buffer is eliminated. And in order to relax the overhead of CIS, conventional correlating-double-sampling is moved to Computation Module. Moreover, the architecture is also dynamic-configurable, which is optimized specifically for CIS data flow. Simulations with HSPICE show that the peak energy efficiency of proposed architecture can achieve 13.91 TOPS/W at the 8-bit percision of multiplication-and-accumulation analog computation, while accuracy loss is only about 5.66%.
